final class Instance
Public API: explicitly declared with @visibility public.

An in-memory MySQL server: its databases, its global variables, and the sessions connected to it.

Statements are parsed by SQL Parser with the grammar of the emulated release, resolved by SQL Semantics against the tables of the server, and executed over rows held in memory. Nothing is written to disk; the server lives as long as this object.

public function __construct(
    public string $version = '8.4.7',
    array<string, string|int> $globals = [],
    list<string> $databases = [],
    public string|null $clientHost = null,
    public bool $supervised = true,
    array<string, array{int, int}> $routineTimestamps = [],
)
source§

A server of MySQL 5.6 or 5.7 starts with latin1 connections, as it greets its clients in latin1 (verified on live 5.6.51 and 5.7.44 servers).

Parameters

$versionstringThe MySQL release emulated, as `8.4.7`
$globalsarray<string, string|int>Global variable values the server starts with, by name
$databaseslist<string>Databases created at start, besides the system ones
$clientHoststring|nullThe host every client is seen connecting from, or null for its address
$supervisedboolWhether a supervisor permits SQL RESTART
$routineTimestampsarray<string, array{int, int}>Installation creation and modification epochs, keyed by FUNCTION:name or PROCEDURE:name

public function restart(): void
source§

Restarts under a supervisor, retaining durable tables and reloading the startup configuration.

Open transactions roll back, session state disappears and MEMORY tables lose their rows. Source: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/restart.html, https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/memory-storage-engine.html.
